newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-OTC Bund investors wary of market top.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-OTC Bund investors wary of market top.

text.p: Investors in over-the-counter (OTC) Bund options are continuing to buy protection against a reversal in the bubbly German market in the new year, OTC traders said on Wednesday.
Investors were reluctant to go short volatility with both the cash and futures market looking toppy, preferring to take a more cautious stance, they said.
"It's the same trend we've seen the last couple of weeks," said an OTC broker at a German bank in Frankfurt.
"People are still looking for six to twelve months options on the put side as protection for next year and on the call side as a replacement for cash," he said.

The broker quoted one-month yield volatility on 10-year cash Bunds at 13.70 percent, slightly off levels earlier in the week. Yield volatility of three and six month options was steady at 12.40 percent while 12 month volatility was at 12.00 percent.

Bund cash yields have been dropping since June, slipping under the psychological 6.0 percent level in early November as the Bundesbank keeps interest rates low to help revive the struggling German economy.
At 1340 GMT, the 10-year benchmark Bund was quoted at a yield of 5.77 percent and a price of 103.33.
Futures markets have also soared higher. December Bund futures on LIFFE hit a new all time high of 101.56 in early trade but had slipped down to 101.46 by afternoon, up 0.09 on the day.

"The shorter end is a bit under pressure because of the Thanksgiving holiday in America," the broker said. "Basically people think Thursday and Friday will be a non-event so they are selling short-dated options to get the time decay."
U.S. markets close early Wednesday and Friday.
Geert Planke, OTC Bund options trader at Paribas in London said however, this strategy may not be prudent going into the Christmas period as liquidity thins.
"With liquidty going out of the market you sometimes get big moves," he said.
"All these people who trade short gamma still have to be relatively careful. Two years ago over Christmas the market dropped one and a half points because there was just no liquidity in it," he said.
He said trade in the OTC Bund futures market was quiet on Wednesday, as it has been in the last few months.
"There was a big seller of the January 101.00 straddle but otherwise it's been extremely quiet. Volatility has been trading at 5.00 percent and is relatively flat on all the months," he said.
